headline: Islanders’ Maccelli, Ritchie to miss time with lower-body injuries
take:
Per Daily Faceoff, Islanders forwards Maccelli and Ritchie both suffered lower-body injuries during New York's 4-1 win over the Leafs on Saturday, and the outlet reports both will miss time.

The Islanders can ill afford losing bodies, because their record (4-3-1) is running ahead of how they've played. So far this season, New York has generated 44.3% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in its games, meaning opponents have had the better of the chances more often than not. At five-on-five the picture is closer to even, at 49%, so the lean comes from elsewhere. The cushion has been goaltending: the Islanders sit at 11 goals saved above expected, which is how many more goals their goalies have stopped than the shots faced would typically allow. They are also 1.8 goals ahead of their expected total. That kind of goaltending can carry a team for a while, but it is hard to count on, and a thinner lineup makes it harder still. Toronto, at 45.7% of expected goals, has been similarly outplayed but has gotten far less help in net (2.2 goals saved above expected).
